Supports four operations: slug lookup, frontmatter filter (with `where` predicates validated against the schema), 1-hop wikilink graph, and substring/regex text search. Strictly read-only — never writes to the vault, never creates cache files. Returns a retrieval report with matches, schema validation status, and filter audit trail. Use when a calling skill needs to check "does this vault already have an answer / claim / context for X?" before doing expensive external work. Schema-strict and fail-closed — invalid queries are rejected rather than returning misleading results.

collector.name: collector
collector.description: Orchestrate all things collecting — authentication and provenance, grading and condition, storage and insurance, market intelligence and portfolio allocation, plus the irreducible vertical knowledge of comics, cards, art, wine, books, watches, coins, memorabilia, and the Tier 2 assets (vinyl, whiskey, handbags, sealed video games, posters, sealed toys, stamps). Activate when a question touches collecting in any form: a book in hand, a card to grade, a painting to authenticate, a cellar to build, a portfolio to allocate, a sale to time. The Collector reads the user's lens (connoisseur or allocator), reads the axis of the question (vertical asset class or horizontal discipline), and routes accordingly.

authentication-provenance.name: authentication-provenance
authentication-provenance.description: Verify that an object is what the seller claims and that its chain of ownership corroborates the attribution. Use when buying any high-value collectible, when an item's history has gaps, when forensic analysis is being considered, when a Certificate of Authenticity is in hand (or conspicuously missing), or when a piece's provenance is being assembled for sale, donation, or insurance. Authentication is the foundation that grading and pricing both sit on top of — skip it and the rest of the analysis becomes decoration.

grading-condition.name: grading-condition
grading-condition.description: Convert object condition into a single tradable number — the codified language that makes illiquid heterogeneous objects fungible in a market. Use when the user is grading, regrading, comparing graded items across services, deciding whether to press or crack out, or trying to understand why a CGC 9.8 trades differently from a PSA 10 even though both sound "perfect." Covers the major scales (CGC, PSA, BGS, SGC, Sheldon, Goldmine, ABAA, WATA) and the cottage industry that grades roughly 14M+ cards a year.

market-intelligence.name: market-intelligence
market-intelligence.description: Price illiquid collectibles using completed-sales data, named indices, and auction-house math. Use when valuing a piece for purchase, sale, insurance, or donation; reading auction comps; computing all-in cost from hammer price; or interpreting cross-asset indices (Liv-ex, PWCC 500, Mei Moses, Knight Frank Luxury Investment Index). Covers buyer's premium tables, liquidity tiers, the bid-ask spread on illiquid assets, and the "sold not asking" discipline that separates real comps from noise.

storage-preservation.name: storage-preservation
storage-preservation.description: Halt physical degradation through climate control, archival materials, and conservation ethics. Use when setting up storage for a new acquisition, evaluating an existing storage environment, choosing between home storage and a freeport / professional facility, or deciding whether to commission conservation on an existing piece. Covers temperature and humidity targets, UV thresholds, Oddy / PAT material testing, and the museum-grade "don't touch it" doctrine.

insurance-risk.name: insurance-risk
insurance-risk.description: Insure and underwrite the handling chain for high-value collectibles via scheduled personal property riders, fine arts policies, and transit cover. Use when scheduling new acquisitions, reviewing existing coverage, evaluating freeport storage, comparing agreed-value vs replacement-cost policies, or after an appraisal update. Covers the major specialty carriers (Chubb Masterpiece, AIG Private Client, PURE, Berkley One, Distinguished, Lloyd's syndicates) and the loss-prevention engineering that real fine arts policies underwrite.

tax-estate-legal.name: tax-estate-legal
tax-estate-legal.description: Navigate the US tax, estate, and legal regime for collectibles — including the 28% maximum long-term capital gains rate on collectibles (IRC §1(h)(4)), Form 8283 qualified-appraisal rules for charitable contributions, IRC §1014 step-up in basis at death, CITES/Lacey Act trade restrictions, AML reporting thresholds, and the death of §1031 exchanges for collectibles post-TCJA. Use when planning a sale, donation, estate transfer, charitable gift, international shipment of regulated materials, or large cash transaction.

portfolio-allocation.name: portfolio-allocation
portfolio-allocation.description: Treat the collection as part of a balance sheet — sizing, concentration, diversification, illiquidity premium, deaccessioning calendar. Use when sizing collectibles against net worth, diversifying within a single asset class, evaluating concentration risk in a single artist or vintage, planning a multi-year deaccessioning strategy, or framing the collection within a whole-net-worth allocation alongside equities, fixed income, real estate, and private markets.

vetting-services.name: vetting-services
vetting-services.description: Vet the appraisers, graders, dealers, and auction houses themselves. Use when selecting an appraiser for tax / insurance / estate purposes, deciding which grading service to send a raw item to, evaluating a dealer's credentials, reading auction-house lot descriptions for what is *not* said, or interpreting attribution language. Covers USPAP compliance, the AAA/ASA/ISA appraiser credentials, CINOA/ADAA dealer associations, and the attribution hierarchy that catalog language uses to encode warranty exposure.

fraud-intelligence.name: fraud-intelligence
fraud-intelligence.description: A pattern library of named scandals, forgery vectors, and red flag clusters across collecting domains. Use when a piece's story sounds too good, when provenance is suspiciously fresh, when a deal is meaningfully below comparable market, when a dealer's behavior triggers caution, or when modern AI-generated provenance is suspected. Covers Knoedler, Kurniawan, Mastro/Wagner, Operation Bullpen, the PSA reholder scandal, the CGC defamation case, and the recurring patterns these scandals reveal.

buying-mechanics.name: buying-mechanics
buying-mechanics.description: Execute acquisitions tactically — auction protocol, max-bid setting, bid increments, the snipe-vs-jump-bid distinction, allocations at retail boutiques, phone-bidding etiquette. Use when about to bid on an auction lot, evaluating a private-treaty negotiation, deciding between live / phone / online / sniper bidding, or trying to acquire a waitlisted retail item (Rolex Daytona, Patek 5711, Birkin). Action skill — workflow-driven.

selling-deaccessioning.name: selling-deaccessioning
selling-deaccessioning.description: Execute sales tactically — channel selection (auction vs dealer vs direct), consignment terms, reserve setting, guarantees and irrevocable bids, the tax-loss vs charitable trade-off. Use when planning a sale, deaccessioning part of a collection, executing a multi-year deaccessioning calendar, or comparing major-house consignment vs private treaty vs direct-to-collector channels. Action skill — workflow-driven.

discovery-sourcing.name: discovery-sourcing
discovery-sourcing.description: Find collectible objects across the channel landscape — estate sales, regional auction houses, major-house aggregators, eBay/WhatNot, Discord/Instagram communities, picker networks. Use when looking for a specific piece, building a sourcing pipeline, evaluating channel-category fit, or learning where the under-priced supply lives. Action skill — workflow-driven.

comics.name: comics
comics.description: Route comics and graphic-novel collecting questions — age categorization (Golden / Silver / Bronze / Copper / Modern), CGC and CBCS grading, pressing economics, key issues and first appearances, restoration disclosure, market venues (Heritage, ComicConnect, ComicLink), and manga / tankōbon as a distinct sub-discipline. Activate when the question concerns a specific issue, a grade decision, a pressing-vs-not decision, a key-issue identification, or any Western or Japanese comics topic.

ages-and-keys.name: ages-and-keys
ages-and-keys.description: Identify and value the canonical key issues across Golden / Silver / Bronze / Copper / Modern ages — first appearances, origin issues, #1s, and major character milestones. Use when asked whether a specific comic is "important," when reading auction listings, when building or evaluating a key-issue-centric collection, or when distinguishing first prints from later printings. The hardest single skill in Western comics: knowing which issues actually matter.

grading-pressing.name: grading-pressing
grading-pressing.description: Decide whether to grade, press, or crack-out a comic — the economic logic of submitting raw, pressing before resubmission, and the disclosure ethics of conservation vs restoration. Use when holding a raw key issue, when a CGC slab is below its likely true grade, or when evaluating a 9.4 → 9.6 / 9.8 pressing-and-resubmit decision. Mirrors crackout ROI from the horizontal grading-condition skill, applied to comic-specific scales and venues.

comics-market.name: comics-market
comics-market.description: Navigate the comics market — venues (Heritage, ComicConnect, ComicLink, eBay, Pristine), reading population reports, comp analysis, the realities of liquidity in CGC-graded vs raw, the "fresh to market" premium on Golden Age, and the special economics of trophy keys at Heritage Signature sales. Use when buying, selling, or pricing a specific issue.

manga-tankobon.name: manga-tankobon
manga-tankobon.description: Navigate manga and tankōbon collecting — first-print Japanese tankōbon, obi (paper waistband) economics, signed shikishi, Mandarake / Suruga-ya / Yahoo Japan venues, the distinction between English first editions and Japanese first prints, and the under-codified authentication landscape that's only now being formalized by CGC's recent entry into the category.

cards.name: cards
cards.description: Route trading-card collecting questions across the four major sub-disciplines — sports cards (PSA/BGS/SGC ecosystem, vintage T206 through junk-wax through modern), Pokémon (1st Ed / Shadowless, JP trophy cards), Magic: The Gathering (Reserved List, NM/LP/MP/HP scale, Alpha/Beta/Unlimited), and other TCGs (Yu-Gi-Oh, Lorcana, Flesh & Blood). Activate when the question touches any trading-card domain. The four sub-skills share grading infrastructure but each has distinct irreducible knowledge.

sports-cards.name: sports-cards
sports-cards.description: Navigate sports card collecting — baseball, basketball, football, hockey — across vintage (T206, 1933 Goudey, 1952 Topps), the "junk wax" caution (1987–1994), and the modern era. Covers PSA / BGS / SGC grading dynamics, centering as the silent killer of modern grades, population reports, and the Heritage / PWCC / Goldin / Fanatics Collect venue landscape.

pokemon-cards.name: pokemon-cards
pokemon-cards.description: Navigate Pokémon card collecting — 1st Edition vs Shadowless vs Unlimited Base Set, Japanese trophy cards (Pikachu Illustrator, No Rarity, Trainer Promos), modern era WOTC vs Pokémon Co., PSA / CGC grading dynamics, and the canonical 1999 Charizard. Pokémon is the largest non-sports trading-card market and has its own grading, authentication, and pricing logic.

mtg-collecting.name: mtg-collecting
mtg-collecting.description: Navigate Magic: The Gathering collecting — the Reserved List, Alpha / Beta / Unlimited distinctions, the NM / LP / MP / HP / DMG condition vocabulary, Power Nine economics, foils, and the dynamics of slabbing MTG (BGS / PSA / CGC). MTG has unique structural elements (the Reserved List policy, the Beta/Unlimited rarity rebalancing) that don't transfer from other TCGs.

tcg-other.name: tcg-other
tcg-other.description: Navigate non-Pokémon, non-MTG trading card games — Yu-Gi-Oh (tournament prize cards, 1st Edition vs Unlimited, ghost rares), Lorcana (Disney/Ravensburger, modern entry), Flesh & Blood, Star Wars TCG, and smaller TCGs. Each TCG has its own scarcity dynamics, grading dynamics, and collector communities. Use when the question is about a non-Pokémon, non-MTG TCG.

books-rare.name: books-rare
books-rare.description: Navigate rare book collecting — first editions, points of issue, dust jacket economics, association copies, the ABAA / ILAB trade-body system, condition vocabulary (As New / Fine / VG / Good / Fair / Poor with separate book and DJ grades), and major venues (Sotheby's, Christie's, Bauman Rare Books, Peter Harrington, Heritage). Use when buying, selling, or evaluating any rare or antiquarian book.

art.name: art
art.description: Route fine-art collecting questions — paintings, prints and multiples, contemporary, Old Masters, photography. Activate when the question touches authentication via catalogue raisonné, attribution hierarchy ("Attributed to" / "Studio of" / "Circle of"), primary vs secondary market dynamics, edition fractions for prints, condition reports for paintings, or the major auction venues (Christie's, Sotheby's, Phillips, Bonhams, Heritage). The most complex of the verticals, requiring discipline across five sub-domains.

paintings.name: paintings
paintings.description: Navigate the painting market — oil, acrylic, watercolor, gouache, mixed-media on canvas, panel, and paper. Use when buying or selling a specific painting, reading a condition report, understanding primary vs secondary market dynamics, or assessing provenance. Covers catalogue raisonné mechanics, the role of conservators, and the major auction venues.

prints-multiples.name: prints-multiples
prints-multiples.description: Navigate the prints and multiples market — limited edition fractions (AP, HC, EA, PP, BAT), the major print techniques (lithograph, etching, silkscreen, woodcut, photogravure), edition size economics, and the Phillips Editions / Christie's Prints / Sotheby's Prints venues. Use when buying, selling, or evaluating any numbered print or multiple by a major artist.

contemporary.name: contemporary
contemporary.description: Navigate contemporary art collecting — primary-market gallery relationships, waiting lists, allocation dynamics, the flipping ethics that govern primary-to-secondary transitions, and the blue-chip versus emerging artist tiers. Use when buying primary from a gallery, evaluating a contemporary work for collection, or understanding why a piece you wanted "wasn't available."

old-masters.name: old-masters
old-masters.description: Navigate the Old Masters market — paintings predating 1800 (broadly), attribution hierarchy discipline, dendrochronology and panel-painting science, multi-century provenance research, and the disciplines unique to this category (cradling, lining history, varnish layering, multiple-hand workshop production). Use when buying, selling, or attributing any painting from before ~1800.

photography.name: photography
photography.description: Navigate fine-art photography collecting — edition sizes, the vintage vs lifetime vs estate print distinction, signature placement conventions (signed-mat vs verso), processes (silver gelatin, platinum, chromogenic, archival pigment), and the major venues (Phillips Photographs, Christie's Photographs, Sotheby's Photographs, Heritage, Swann). Use when buying, selling, or evaluating any fine-art photograph.

wine-collecting.name: wine-collecting
wine-collecting.description: Route wine-collecting questions — en primeur futures, cellar strategy and storage, provenance and ullage assessment, and wine as an asset class (Liv-ex indices, blue-chip producers, illiquidity premium). This is the **collector** view of wine; the **tasting and sensory** view of wine lives in Bacchus. Both suites stay self-contained — this director mirrors Bacchus's wine-market structure rather than cross-linking, by the user's design choice.

en-primeur.name: en-primeur
en-primeur.description: Navigate the en primeur (wine futures) market — Bordeaux's pre-bottling release system, the La Place de Bordeaux négociant infrastructure, the timing and pricing dynamics, and the risks (delivery, vintage quality reassessment, négociant solvency). Use when considering an en primeur purchase, evaluating a future for current-vintage Bordeaux, or understanding why en primeur prices differ from physical bottles.

cellar-strategy.name: cellar-strategy
cellar-strategy.description: Build and manage a collector wine cellar — bonded storage vs home storage, OWC vs loose bottles, drinking windows, deaccessioning timing, the trade-offs between consumption and investment. Use when designing a cellar, deciding where to store, or planning what to drink vs hold vs sell.

wine-provenance.name: wine-provenance
wine-provenance.description: Assess the physical and documentary provenance of wine — ullage, capsule integrity, label condition, cellar source designations (ex-château / ex-cellar / private collection / European collection), and the Kurniawan-era counterfeit risk. Use when buying any wine 20+ years old, when provenance claims are vague, or when bottles surface from unknown sources.

wine-as-asset.name: wine-as-asset
wine-as-asset.description: Wine as an alternative-asset class — Liv-ex indices, blue-chip producers, illiquidity premium, cross-asset correlation, the structural friction in wine investment, and the honest case for wine as a portfolio diversifier rather than a return engine. Mirrors Bacchus's collecting-investment skill under the parallel-mirror design choice; both suites remain self-contained.

watches.name: watches
watches.description: Route timepiece collecting questions — vintage watches (tropical dials, ghost bezels, originality discipline), modern watches (Rolex/Patek/AP allocations, gray market dynamics), and reference-number discipline (double-signed, papers, "full set"). Activate when the question touches authentication of originality, polishing risk, allocation strategy, or any watch identification or valuation.

vintage-watches.name: vintage-watches
vintage-watches.description: Navigate vintage watch collecting — tropical dials, ghost bezels, original lume, the unpolished-case premium, redial detection, and the Paul Newman Daytona benchmark. Use when evaluating any vintage Rolex, Patek, AP, or other pre-2000 watch for purchase or sale.

modern-watches.name: modern-watches
modern-watches.description: Navigate modern watch collecting — Rolex Daytona / GMT-Master, Patek 5711 Nautilus, AP Royal Oak, the allocation game at authorized dealers, gray market dynamics, and the post-2022 market correction. Use when considering a new boutique allocation, weighing gray market premiums, or evaluating modern reference values.

watch-references.name: watch-references
watch-references.description: Decode watch reference numbers, "full set" documentation requirements, double-signed retailer marks (Tiffany, Cartier signature), and the discipline of period-appropriate configuration verification. Use when identifying a specific watch, evaluating completeness of provenance documentation, or assessing reference-specific value drivers.

coins.name: coins
coins.description: Route numismatic questions — US coins (Sheldon 1-70 scale, RD/RB/BN designations, FS/FBL/FH strike designations), world coins (broader category, region-specific markets), and die varieties (1955 DDO, 1969-S DDO, the specialist subfield where die identity matters more than grade). The most codified condition system in collecting via the Sheldon scale.

us-coins.name: us-coins
us-coins.description: Navigate US numismatics — Sheldon scale grades, mint marks (P/D/S/CC/O/W), RD/RB/BN copper designations, CAM/DCAM proof contrast, strike designations (FS/FBL/FH), and the canonical US series (Morgan dollars, Lincoln cents, Walking Liberty halves, Indian Head pennies).

world-coins.name: world-coins
world-coins.description: Navigate world coin collecting — British (sovereigns, crowns, pennies), European (German thalers, French écus, Italian states), Asian (Chinese, Japanese, Korean), ancient coins (Greek, Roman, Byzantine), and the specific authentication and grading challenges of non-US numismatics. Use when buying or evaluating any non-US coin or ancient.

die-varieties.name: die-varieties
die-varieties.description: Navigate the die-variety specialist subfield — doubled dies (1955 DDO, 1969-S DDO), repunched mint marks (RPM), overdates, and other minting errors that create coins with values disproportionate to their date/mintmark. The variety, not the date, is sometimes the asset.

memorabilia.name: memorabilia
memorabilia.description: Route memorabilia and autograph questions — sports autographs (PSA/DNA, JSA, BAS), game-used and game-worn (photo-matched, team-letter, player-issued), and pop-culture memorabilia (props, costumes, signed music/film items). Activate when authenticating signatures, game-used items, or pop culture provenance.

autographs.name: autographs
autographs.description: Navigate autograph collecting — sports, entertainment, and historical signatures. Covers PSA/DNA, JSA, BAS authentication tiers, the witnessed-vs-opinion distinction, common forgery vectors (Mantle, Ruth, Cobb, Babe Ruth's specific signature evolution), and the major venues (Heritage, Goldin, Lelands, REA).

game-used.name: game-used
game-used.description: Navigate game-used and game-worn memorabilia — photo-matched (the trophy tier), team-letter authenticated, player-issued. Use when evaluating jerseys, bats, balls, equipment, and the tiers of authentication that determine value. Covers MEARS, Resolution Photomatching, and the major sports authenticators.

pop-culture.name: pop-culture
pop-culture.description: Navigate film, TV, and music memorabilia — production-used props, screen-worn costumes, signed instruments, original concert artifacts. Covers Profiles in History, Heritage Entertainment Auctions, and Julien's, plus the specific authentication landscape for Hollywood and music memorabilia (which is less centralized than sports).

vinyl-records.name: vinyl-records
vinyl-records.description: Navigate vinyl record collecting — Goldmine grading, matrix/runout numbers identifying first pressings, deadwax codes, mono vs stereo, country-of-pressing premiums (UK first-press Beatles, Japanese audiophile pressings), and the Mobile Fidelity / Analogue Productions audiophile reissue market.

whiskey-collecting.name: whiskey-collecting
whiskey-collecting.description: Navigate whiskey collecting — Macallan (the Rolex of Scotch), Pappy Van Winkle, Japanese whisky (Yamazaki, Karuizawa), the Rare Whisky 101 indices, the major auction venues (Sotheby's, Bonhams Whisky, Whisky Auctioneer), and the cask-investment fraud red flags.

luxury-handbags.name: luxury-handbags
luxury-handbags.description: Navigate luxury handbag collecting — Hermès Birkin and Kelly authentication via blind stamps, leather grammar (Togo, Epsom, Box, Chèvre, exotic), hardware (PHW palladium vs GHW gold), resale venues (Privé Porter, Madison Avenue Couture, Sotheby's Luxury, Christie's Handbags). Use when authenticating, valuing, or sourcing any Hermès trophy bag or other luxury handbag.

video-games-sealed.name: video-games-sealed
video-games-sealed.description: Navigate sealed retro video game collecting — WATA / VGA / CGC grading services, the seal rating system (C through A++), Heritage Auctions venue dominance, the 2020-2021 record sales (Super Mario 64 at $1.56M), and the post-2022 market correction. Use when evaluating sealed retro games or considering grading.

movie-posters.name: movie-posters
movie-posters.description: Navigate movie poster collecting — one-sheets (27×41" canonical US format), inserts (14×36"), half-sheets (22×28"), lobby cards, the C1-C10 grading scale (Jon Warren's standard), linen-backing conservation, and the major venues (Heritage Movie Poster sales).

sealed-toys-lego.name: sealed-toys-lego
sealed-toys-lego.description: Navigate sealed toys and LEGO collecting — MISB (Mint In Sealed Box), box preservation as ~30-40% of value, BrickEconomy as the pricing reference, the UCS Millennium Falcon (10179) as canonical, and the broader vintage sealed toy market (Star Wars Kenner, Transformers G1, GI Joe). Use when evaluating sealed boxed toys for purchase or sale.

stamps-philately.name: stamps-philately
stamps-philately.description: Navigate philatelic collecting — MNH (Mint Never Hinged) vs MH (Mint Hinged) vs Used, Scott / Stanley Gibbons / Michel / Yvert catalog references, expertization (PF / PSE), errors and varieties (inverted Jenny, color shifts), and the trophy world rarities. Use when buying, selling, or evaluating any stamp collection above hobby tier.

360-feedback-design.name: 360-feedback-design
360-feedback-design.description: Design and run a personal 360 — selecting raters, drafting questions, running the process, synthesizing the report, and integrating the findings. Reference when approaching a major transition, periodically calibrating self-perception against peer perception, or auditing whether current behaviors match intentions. A well-run 360 every 18–24 months is the single most useful feedback instrument for senior professionals.

advisor-board.name: advisor-board
advisor-board.description: Construct and maintain a personal advisory board — the small group of trusted advisors who deliver hard truths, deep pattern-recognition, and high-trust feedback. Reference when building the advisor set for the first time, refreshing the composition, or designing the cadence and ask structure. The personal advisory board is the single highest-leverage feedback channel a senior professional has.

audience-tuning.name: audience-tuning
audience-tuning.description: Tune the same underlying narrative for different audiences — clinical peer, recruiter, hiring manager, VC partner, board chair, founder, journalist — without distorting truth. Reference when preparing a version of materials for a specific audience, when the user has multiple parallel processes targeting different archetypes, or when feedback suggests the message landed wrong for the audience. Audience tuning is selection, not distortion.

behavioral-frameworks.name: behavioral-frameworks
behavioral-frameworks.description: Build and use behavioral interview frameworks — STAR, CAR, and the story-bank approach. Map common behavioral probes to a small set of pre-rehearsed stories so the user is never improvising under pressure. Reference when preparing for any interview round that includes "tell me about a time" questions, building or refreshing a story bank, or diagnosing why current behavioral answers aren't landing.

board-readiness.name: board-readiness
board-readiness.description: Prepare for board service — observer or director — covering fiduciary literacy, board meeting protocol, IC dynamics, governance roles, the relationship between board and CEO, and the practices that distinguish effective board members from passive ones. Reference when offered a board observer or director seat, preparing for board work in a CMO or operator role, or building toward board candidacy.

cold-outreach.name: cold-outreach
cold-outreach.description: Craft and send cold emails or DMs to people you do not yet know — partners, founders, operators, recruiters. Reference when reaching out to someone in your target ecosystem for the first time, asking for a 30-minute conversation, or attempting to convert a cold contact into a warm relationship. Cold outreach is craft, not luck — the strong message is short, specific, and asks for something the recipient can say yes to in 30 seconds.

cover-letter-craft.name: cover-letter-craft
cover-letter-craft.description: Draft firm-specific, thesis-aware cover letters for VC, operator, board, and advisory applications. Reference when applying for any role where a cover letter is required or optional-but-strategic. The strong cover letter is the highest-ROI artifact in a senior search: 30 minutes of work that demonstrates diligence, judgment, and reading-the-firm, and that distinguishes the user from the 95% who submit generic letters.

credibility-translation.name: credibility-translation
credibility-translation.description: Translate clinical, academic, and trial-development credentials into the operator, investor, or board vocabulary the target audience parses. Reference when rewriting bullets for a non-clinical audience, preparing to explain trial work to a VC, or auditing whether the audience can recognize the value of the user's experience. Untranslated credibility is invisible to the wrong audience — and the wrong audience is most audiences outside clinical settings.

domain-deepdives.name: domain-deepdives
domain-deepdives.description: Prepare for domain-technical interview rounds — the rounds where the user will be tested on what they claim to know (clinical development, regulatory strategy, asset evaluation, trial design). Reference when preparing for a clinical depth interview, a VC diligence round, a CMO scientific scrutiny round, or any conversation where the interviewer will probe technical mastery. The senior interviewer is testing reasoning under uncertainty, not encyclopedic recall.

ecosystem-mapping.name: ecosystem-mapping
ecosystem-mapping.description: Map the target ecosystem you are entering — firms, operators, advisors, founders, publications, conferences, and the relationships between them. Reference when starting a search in a new ecosystem (biotech VC, board candidates, specific therapeutic area), preparing for a firm-specific interview, or building a relationship plan. The map is the foundation that makes all other network activity efficient.

equity-literacy.name: equity-literacy
equity-literacy.description: Understand and negotiate equity grants — options vs RSUs vs PSUs, strike price, vesting, cliff, refresh, acceleration, dilution, secondary, 409A. Reference when evaluating an equity grant, modeling expected value across scenarios, or negotiating equity terms. Most senior comp upside lives in equity; getting equity wrong dwarfs getting base wrong. Equity literacy is the foundation of every senior negotiation.

executive-communication.name: executive-communication
executive-communication.description: Write at executive grade — memos, decks, board materials, decision recommendations, status updates — using BLUF structure, audience-tuned vocabulary, and explicit reasoning. Reference when drafting any document that will be read by a senior audience under time pressure. Executive communication is the highest-leverage written skill in any senior role: one good memo creates an artifact that travels across the organization and lives for months.

executive-interview-prep.name: executive-interview-prep
executive-interview-prep.description: Prepare for executive-level interviews — CMO, Head of Clinical Development, SVP, Chief Medical Officer at startups, scale-ups, and growth-stage biotechs. Cover the canonical executive interview elements — strategic thinking, P&L judgment, leadership scenarios, "first 90 days" plans, and board-readiness. Reference when prepping for any executive loop, building a 100-day plan presentation, or rehearsing leadership-scenario answers.

executive-presence.name: executive-presence
executive-presence.description: Direct executive communication, meeting mastery, public speaking, and board readiness to the appropriate specialist skill. Activate when the user is preparing to *show up* at an executive level — running a meeting, presenting to a board, giving a conference talk, writing an exec memo, or stepping into a board-adjacent role. Executive presence is the discipline of being read as senior when you are in the room, in print, and on stage.

exit-and-transition.name: exit-and-transition
exit-and-transition.description: Negotiate exit terms — notice, garden leave, severance, non-compete carveouts, IP releases, transition consulting, references. Reference when leaving a role (voluntary or involuntary), planning the timing of a departure, or evaluating an exit package. Exit negotiations have legal dimensions and high downstream consequences; the terms negotiated here shape what the next move looks like.

feedback-loops.name: feedback-loops
feedback-loops.description: Direct 360 feedback design, performance review craft, personal advisory board, and reflection and journaling to the appropriate specialist skill. Activate when the user is designing how they collect, structure, and metabolize feedback — running a 360, drafting a self-assessment, building a personal advisory board, or maintaining a reflection practice. Feedback loops are the discipline that turns experience into compounding judgment.

idp-and-okrs.name: idp-and-okrs
idp-and-okrs.description: Build personal OKRs and individual development plans (IDPs) — making the trajectory measurable so that progress is visible and adjustments are timely. Reference at year-end planning, quarterly reviews, after a 360, or when the trajectory feels intentional but unmeasured. Without measurable goals, trajectory drifts; with measurable goals tied to the right time-horizon, intentional career-building compounds.

interview-mastery.name: interview-mastery
interview-mastery.description: Direct behavioral interview prep, domain-technical deep-dives, VC interviews, executive interviews, and panel/case interviews to the appropriate specialist skill. Activate when the user is preparing for any interview that matters — first conversations, IC pitches, partner interviews, board candidate screens, or executive panels. Interview mastery is the discipline of rehearsing the conversation before it happens, with the right framework for the format.

introductions-and-referrals.name: introductions-and-referrals
introductions-and-referrals.description: Ask for, give, and track introductions and referrals — the warm-intro economy that drives most senior moves. Reference when asking a connector for an intro, offering an intro to someone in your network, deciding whether to refer a candidate, or building a tracking system for outstanding intros. Warm intros convert at 70–90% vs cold outreach at 25–40%; the leverage is real, and the craft is in not abusing it.

linkedin-optimization.name: linkedin-optimization
linkedin-optimization.description: Optimize LinkedIn for the named trajectory — headline, About, featured section, experience bullets, recommendations, and activity strategy. Reference when refreshing the profile for a search, increasing recruiter visibility, or aligning the profile with a newly-architected narrative. LinkedIn is the search engine of professional life; what is not searchable about you on LinkedIn does not exist for most opportunity flow.

meeting-mastery.name: meeting-mastery
meeting-mastery.description: Run and contribute to meetings at executive level — agenda design, opening moves, decision protocols, derailment recovery, follow-ups. Reference when designing a high-stakes meeting, recovering a meeting that's going off the rails, or auditing why your meetings feel low-leverage. Most senior work happens in meetings; the ability to *run* a meeting is what separates senior from staff in a way that's visible to everyone in the room.

mentor.name: mentor
mentor.description: Orchestrate professional development across personal positioning, interview mastery, network cultivation, trajectory design, executive presence, negotiation leverage, and feedback loops. Activate when the question concerns career strategy, role transitions, resume or cover letter craft, interview preparation (job, executive, VC, board), personal branding, mentorship, networking, OKRs/IDPs, or compensation. Mentor reads the user's context, infers the career stage, and routes to the right director — with a dual-track teaching convention so every answer is both a self-coaching tool and a teach-others artifact.

mentorship-design.name: mentorship-design
mentorship-design.description: Design and maintain mentorship relationships — finding mentors, structuring asks, setting cadence, building reciprocity, and exiting with grace when the relationship has run its course. Reference when seeking a mentor for a specific transition, formalizing an informal mentorship, or learning to be a mentor for others. Mentorship is not a transaction; it is a relationship with structure.

narrative-architecture.name: narrative-architecture
narrative-architecture.description: Build and refresh the underlying career narrative — the through-line that ties past decisions to future trajectory and gives every surface (resume, LinkedIn, cover letter, interview answer) a coherent center. Reference when starting a search, navigating a pivot, or noticing that artifacts read inconsistently. A narrative without architecture is biography; a narrative with architecture is a thesis a sophisticated audience can endorse in 30 seconds.

negotiation-leverage.name: negotiation-leverage
negotiation-leverage.description: Direct offer negotiation, equity literacy, title and scope negotiation, and exit / transition craft to the appropriate specialist skill. Activate when the user is negotiating any term — base, bonus, equity, title, scope, signing bonus, vesting, severance, non-compete, garden leave, or notice. Negotiation leverage is the discipline of converting earned credibility into terms that protect the trajectory's optionality.

network-cultivation.name: network-cultivation
network-cultivation.description: Direct cold outreach, relationship stewardship, mentorship design, ecosystem mapping, and introductions / referrals to the appropriate specialist skill. Activate when the user is building or maintaining the relationships that compound into opportunities — sending a first email to a partner, designing a mentor cadence, mapping a venture ecosystem, asking for or giving an introduction. The compounding asset of a career is a small number of high-trust relationships, not a large number of weak ones.

offer-negotiation.name: offer-negotiation
offer-negotiation.description: Negotiate incoming offers — base, bonus, signing bonus, performance metrics, start date, relocation, benefits — using collaborative-problem-solving frame and explicit BATNA reasoning. Reference when an offer arrives, when a counter-proposal needs drafting, or when the user is deciding whether and how to push back. The most expensive career mistake is not negotiating; the second most expensive is negotiating from the wrong frame.

optionality-architecture.name: optionality-architecture
optionality-architecture.description: Evaluate career choices by their effect on the option set — which doors does this open, which doors does it close, what's the reversibility, how path-dependent is the future you're constructing. Reference when weighing a specific decision (this offer vs that offer; pivot now vs later; specialist vs generalist), at annual planning time, or whenever a decision feels weightier than next-paycheck logic suggests.

panel-and-case.name: panel-and-case
panel-and-case.description: Prepare for panel interviews, live cases, working sessions, take-home cases, and IC simulations. Reference when the loop includes any multi-interviewer dynamic or live problem-solving format. The behaviors that win solo interviews are not the same as those that win panels and cases — these formats require deliberate preparation in multi-rater dynamics, live structured thinking, and visible collaboration.

performance-review-craft.name: performance-review-craft
performance-review-craft.description: Write self-assessments, prepare for review conversations, calibrate against rubrics, and "manage up" the formal review process. Reference at year-end review time, mid-cycle review, or when preparing for promotion / leveling discussions. The formal review is a high-stakes artifact that affects comp, advancement, and reputation; treating it as a checkbox loses significant career upside.

personal-positioning.name: personal-positioning
personal-positioning.description: Direct narrative architecture, LinkedIn optimization, public portfolio strategy, credibility translation, audience tuning, resume craft, and cover letter craft to the right specialist skill. Activate when the user is shaping how they show up to a target audience — refreshing a resume, drafting a cover letter, rewriting a LinkedIn About, deciding what to publish on GitHub, or translating clinical credibility for non-clinical audiences. Personal positioning is the discipline of being legible to the rooms you want to enter.

pivot-sequencing.name: pivot-sequencing
pivot-sequencing.description: Design multi-year transition plans — what to do in year 1 to make year 3 possible, intermediate roles, advisor seats, side artifacts, and the order that makes the move credible. Reference when the target archetype is multi-year away, when an obvious direct-path is unavailable, or when the user is choosing between fast-and-risky and slow-and-credible paths. Most senior pivots are not single moves; they are sequences.

public-portfolio.name: public-portfolio
public-portfolio.description: Strategize what to publish on GitHub, blog, or other public surfaces as proof-of-thinking artifacts that compound credibility over time. Reference when deciding what to make public, curating an existing portfolio, or evaluating whether a piece of work merits a public artifact. The asymmetric leverage of senior professionals is that one good public artifact becomes part of the credibility you draw on for years.

public-speaking.name: public-speaking
public-speaking.description: Prepare and deliver public talks — conference keynotes, panel appearances, podcast interviews, fireside chats, and high-stakes presentations. Reference when preparing for any external-facing speaking engagement, building a talk from scratch, or improving delivery from prior recordings. Public speaking is a trainable craft, not a personality trait — the senior speakers were rarely born to it; they rehearsed.

reflection-and-journaling.name: reflection-and-journaling
reflection-and-journaling.description: Maintain a reflection practice — daily, weekly, quarterly — that turns experience into nameable, retrievable lessons. Reference when starting a reflection practice, recovering one that's lapsed, structuring quarterly retrospectives, or integrating findings from 360s and advisor sessions. Without reflection, experience doesn't produce wisdom by default; the same lessons re-recur every 18 months until the career stalls.

relationship-stewardship.name: relationship-stewardship
relationship-stewardship.description: Maintain and deepen warm professional relationships over months and years through signal-driven cadence, light CRM, and high-value touchpoint craft. Reference when re-warming a cold relationship, designing a stewardship rhythm for the relationships that matter, or auditing why current relationships feel transactional. Stewardship is the unit of work that compounds a senior career — most relationships die from neglect, not from rupture.

resume-craft.name: resume-craft
resume-craft.description: Build and refresh a resume — convert an academic CV to an industry resume, draft and edit outcome-led bullets, tailor to a specific JD, produce one-page and two-page variants. Reference when starting a search, refreshing materials, or preparing for a specific application. The physician CV is a record; the industry resume is a positioning artifact. The conversion is its own discipline.

role-archetype-mapping.name: role-archetype-mapping
role-archetype-mapping.description: Name the target role archetype precisely — what each archetype actually does day-to-day, what credentials it requires, what tradeoffs it imposes, and where each archetype sits in the broader career landscape. Reference when choosing among targets (operator vs investor vs founder vs advisor vs board), preparing materials for a specific archetype, or sanity-checking that the archetype matches the user's actual goals. The mapping is the first move in trajectory design.

skill-gap-analysis.name: skill-gap-analysis
skill-gap-analysis.description: Name the gap between the user's current skill stack and the target role archetype's requirements, then design the smallest credible action to close each gap. Reference when evaluating readiness for a target role, planning a multi-year build, or auditing why current applications aren't converting. Honest gap analysis is the foundation of growth; most stalled trajectories are stalled because gaps are unnamed.

title-and-scope.name: title-and-scope
title-and-scope.description: Negotiate title, level, reporting line, scope, charter, headcount, and budget — the structural levers that shape what the role actually is over its tenure. Reference when evaluating an offer, considering a re-org or scope expansion in a current role, or weighing title vs scope tradeoffs. Title is mostly a future-signal; scope is mostly a current-reality. Both are negotiable; both compound.

trajectory-design.name: trajectory-design
trajectory-design.description: Direct role-archetype mapping, optionality architecture, IDPs and OKRs, skill-gap analysis, and pivot sequencing to the appropriate specialist skill. Activate when the user is making or remaking the underlying choice of *what career to build* — picking a target role archetype, designing optionality, setting personal OKRs, naming skill gaps, sequencing a multi-year pivot. Trajectory design is the strategic layer that every other career activity serves.

vc-interview-prep.name: vc-interview-prep
vc-interview-prep.description: Prepare for VC interviews across associate, principal, partner, venture-partner, EIR, and operating-partner roles. Cover the canonical VC interview elements — market thesis, deal review, portfolio reasoning, "why VC," fit questions, and the IC simulation. Reference when prepping for any VC firm interview, building thesis materials, or rehearsing deal-review answers. VC associate pools are dominated by consulting and finance backgrounds; MD-operators are differentiated but unfamiliar — preparation must explicitly translate the value.

bias-and-funding-tracer.name: bias-and-funding-tracer
bias-and-funding-tracer.description: Trace funding sources, author conflicts of interest, and institutional incentives behind a set of sources. Use when source quality alone is insufficient — when "10 sources agree" might mean "10 sources funded by the same company agree." Especially load-bearing for biotech (industry-funded trials), markets (sell-side analyst incentives), and politically charged topics. Plugged into Phase 3 of Spelunker after source-triangulator completes its sweep.

paywall-strategist.name: paywall-strategist
paywall-strategist.description: Systematically work around source paywalls before tagging a claim Unverifiable. Searches for preprint mirrors (bioRxiv, SSRN, arXiv, institutional repositories), extracts available abstracts, surfaces adjacent open-access work, and generates ask-the-author email templates. Plugged into Spelunker's Reentry Protocol Level 1 — must be exhausted before escalating to Level 2 (decompose further) or tagging the claim Unverifiable.

synthesis-translator.name: synthesis-translator
synthesis-translator.description: Convert a Spelunker research brief into one of four target formats — executive memo, VC pitch bullets, tweet thread, or decision memo — while preserving citations and confidence tags. Spelunker has one default output (long-form brief); this skill multiplies that into the formats the user actually publishes/uses. Callable as the optional last step of Spelunker Phase 6, or standalone on any existing brief in `research/`.

counterfactual-prober.name: counterfactual-prober
counterfactual-prober.description: Active disconfirmation. Given a synthesized brief, generate "if the conclusion were false, what should we observe in the world?" predictions and search for those signatures. Stronger than passive adversarial search ("X debunked"), which only finds what others have already written. Plugged into Spelunker Phase 5 between the existing adversarial search and backpropagation. Triggered in `deep` mode by default; optional in `standard`.

sensory-translation.name: sensory-translation
sensory-translation.description: Translate a worldbuilding sensory palette into prose technique. Use when a built region exists (via `sensory-worldbuilding`) and the user needs to render it on the page without sensory-dump paragraphs. Covers detail-selection, POV attention bias, sensory-as-characterization, and diction-by-region. Sister skill to `world-to-story` and `cultural-voice` — together they form the worldbuilding-to-prose bridge.

cultural-voice.name: cultural-voice
cultural-voice.description: Translate a culture into how its people talk and think on the page — vocabulary domains, idiom source, syntactic rhythm, metaphor reach, and the things characters refuse to explain because everyone they know already understands. Use when a culture has been built (via `cultures-societies` and `naming-system`) and the user needs characters from that culture to *sound* like they belong to it without infodump or accent caricature. Sister skill to `world-to-story` and `sensory-translation` — together they form the worldbuilding-to-prose bridge.

problem-diagnosis.name: problem-diagnosis
problem-diagnosis.description: Route a problem statement to the right diagnostic skill — typology classification, audience detection, stakes assessment, and the mess/wicked reference frameworks. Activate at the start of problem framing (six-eyes Phase 2) when you need a typology + audience + stakes profile before decomposing or reframing. This director owns the "what kind of problem is this, for whom, at what stakes" question.

problem-decomposition.name: problem-decomposition
problem-decomposition.description: Route a diagnosed problem to the right decomposition method — root-cause technique selection and the Polya heuristic catalog. Activate at six-eyes Phase 3 (Decompose), after a typology profile exists, when you need to break a statement into atomic, root-tagged parts before reframing or auditing. This director owns the "break it down to its real components" question.

problem-reframing.name: problem-reframing
problem-reframing.description: Route a decomposed problem to the right reframing technique — alternative formulations, Munger inversion, stakeholder rotation, and the framing-effects reference. Activate at six-eyes Phase 4 (Reframe) when you need to expose that the current formulation is not the only one, or when a statement feels stuck or one-sided. This director owns the "is this even the right framing?" question.

statement-compression.name: statement-compression
statement-compression.description: Route an audited problem statement to the right compression format by audience — BLUF, Minto pyramid, SCQA, or Claude-prompt structure — grounded in the Minto reference. Activate at six-eyes Phase 5 (Compress) once a statement has passed audit and needs to be shaped for a specific reader. This director owns the "say it in the form this audience needs" question.

statement-audit.name: statement-audit
statement-audit.description: Route a candidate problem statement through the audit battery — XY-pattern detection, answerability, falsifiability, scope bounding, and the six-axis grader. Activate at six-eyes Phase 6 (Audit) to catch the standard failure modes before a statement is accepted, and to decide whether the re-state loop must fire. This director owns the "is this statement actually sound?" question.

evidence-gathering.name: evidence-gathering
evidence-gathering.description: Route a research question to the evidence-acquisition skills — claim decomposition, source triangulation, funding/COI tracing, paywall strategy, and the generative agentic-researcher. Activate during spelunker Phases 2–3 (Decompose → Investigate) when a question needs to be broken into claims and each claim backed by independent sources. This director owns the "find and qualify the evidence" half of the research pipeline.

synthesis-verification.name: synthesis-verification
synthesis-verification.description: Route qualified evidence to the synthesis-and-verification skills — confidence-tagged brief assembly, active counterfactual disconfirmation, and format translation. Activate during spelunker Phases 4–6 (Synthesize → Self-Check → Present) once evidence bundles exist and need to become an honest, gap-aware brief. This director owns the "reason from the evidence and stress-test the conclusion" half of the research pipeline.

data-generation-monitor.name: data-generation-monitor
data-generation-monitor.description: Read each new functional-genomics data-engine release as a forward signal of pre-validated drug targets. Tracks pQTL/MR/colocalization atlases (UKB-PPP, deCODE), DepMap dependency updates, genome-scale and spatial Perturb-seq, prime-editing/SGE variant screens, optical pooled screens, biobank releases (FinnGen, All of Us, MVP), and organoid biobanks. Activate when a new dataset, atlas, or AI-discovery claim drops and you need to know which targets just gained orthogonal causal support — for a scientist learning the field or an investor screening early opportunities.

emerging-target-radar.name: emerging-target-radar
emerging-target-radar.description: Fuse literature/preprint velocity, scientific mindshare, and orthogonal data-engine convergence into a ranked watchlist of emerging target x modality candidates — each tagged with realized/expected literature-to-first-in-human lead time, the responsible NewCo-creation events, and which historical pattern it follows (genetics-first, modality-unlock, or resistance-ladder). Activate when scanning the discovery frontier for what is inflecting before consensus, building or refreshing an early-stage target watchlist, or sourcing candidate objects for downstream arc-placement and conviction scoring.

frontier-conviction-scorer.name: frontier-conviction-scorer
frontier-conviction-scorer.description: Score a discovery-stage target × modality candidate before any clinical PoS exists, decomposing conviction into P(biology holds) × P(modality deliverable) × position-on-arc × competitive-timing, anchored to empirical phase/modality/therapeutic-area base rates rather than management optimism. Activate when ranking pre-clinical programs, sizing the binding risk (biology vs platform vs timing), benchmarking a frontier asset against its class prior, or deciding what to advance — then hand off to rNPV the moment a clinical asset and indication exist.

frontier-intelligence.name: frontier-intelligence
frontier-intelligence.description: Direct frontier signal-scanning, mindshare quantification, data-generation monitoring, and emerging-target radar to the appropriate specialist skill. Activate when the question is "what is emerging?" — which targets and modalities are accreting attention and data before they are drug classes, how fast, and which are worth tracking. This director owns the front of the funnel: it reads the second derivative of the literature, capital, and data-engine signals and emits a ranked watchlist of candidates for the analog engine to place on the historical arc.

mindshare-tracker.name: mindshare-tracker
mindshare-tracker.description: Compute a 0-100 weighted momentum score for an emerging target or modality from conference share-of-voice (AACR/ASCO/ASH/ESMO abstract share, JPM January agenda), financing and NewCo-formation flows, and Altmetric as a calibrated high-noise tripwire. Treats reflexivity as structural and pairs the score with a contrarian froth-vs-merit overlay plus an orthogonal Consensus evidence-maturity gate. Activate when sizing where scientific attention and capital are flowing, whether a theme is pre- or post-consensus, and whether momentum is durable merit or reflexive hype.

moa-analog-engine.name: moa-analog-engine
moa-analog-engine.description: Place a discovery- or early-clinical-stage drug candidate on the historical arc of its mechanism class. Given a target, modality, or mechanism, finds the nearest validated analog among twelve matured classes, names the still-pending ignition trial to watch, dates its position on the five-phase life-cycle, and reads a marquee failure followed by modality re-engineering as a buy signal, not a kill. Activate when asking "what does this mechanism become, how long, and what proves it" — for a clinician learning the field or an investor screening early opportunities.

modality-lifecycle.name: modality-lifecycle
modality-lifecycle.description: Place a therapeutic modality on its maturity arc and answer "is this deliverable yet?" using a live mature-vs-proving map keyed to the delivery unlock as the primary state variable. Produces a modality position read with the binding delivery bottleneck, the platform fix that converts the class, and a P(modality deliverable) term for the conviction scorer. Activate when assessing whether a modality is ready, what gates its next stage, or whether a stalled class is about to inflect — for clinicians learning the field and investors screening early opportunities alike.

modality-trajectory.name: modality-trajectory
modality-trajectory.description: Direct historical MOA-arc placement, modality-lifecycle assessment, human-genetics target validation, and discovery-stage conviction scoring to the appropriate specialist skill. Activate when the question is "where will this go?" — given an emerging target×modality, place it on the trajectory past mechanism classes followed, find its nearest validated analog, grade how validated the target is, and produce an early conviction score. This director is the analog engine: it turns a frontier candidate into a placed, graded, scored thesis that hands off to PoS/rNPV once a clinical asset exists.

signal-scanner.name: signal-scanner
signal-scanner.description: Measure scientific momentum for an emerging target or modality by computing the second derivative (acceleration) of PubMed and bioRxiv/medRxiv volume, citation-burst detection on landmark papers, and author-affiliation concentration to subtract single-lab artifacts, cross-checked against patent velocity, NIH grant flows, and the first-IND translation event. Activate when asking whether a target/modality is inflecting before consensus, how early you are, or when separating a genuine emerging field from review-driven or single-lab hype.

target-validation-ladder.name: target-validation-ladder
target-validation-ladder.description: Grade the human-genetic validation of a drug target on a causality-ranked evidence ladder (Mendelian/rare-variant > coding GWAS+colocalization > Mendelian randomization > non-coding GWAS), scoring direction-of-effect concordance, tractability, and on-target safety read-across. Produces a 0-13 composite tier from Open Targets, the Genetic Priority Score, gnomAD constraint, and a cis-MR/PheWAS scan. Activate when assessing whether a target hypothesis is genetically supported, before mechanism-risk or PoS modeling, when screening an early-discovery asset, or when learning what separates a PCSK9-class target from a hopeful GWAS hit.

quality-critic.name: quality-critic
quality-critic.description: Judge whether a piece of prose is actually good — not whether it is consistent, and not by describing its features, but by ruling PASS/FAIL on a boolean craft rubric with a floor gate. Use after the consistency gate passes, when prose needs an objective quality verdict before revision, when running a generate→critique→refine loop, or when the user asks "is this scene working?" Emits a diagnosis for prose-editor, never a score for the writer to chase.

whole-story-judge.name: whole-story-judge
whole-story-judge.description: Judge whether a whole story works as a whole — not scene by scene. Checks the macro properties that only exist at the level of the complete draft: are the setups paid off, does the arc have a shape, do events connect causally, is the opening's promise kept, is it globally consistent? Use after the scene-level quality gate passes, on a complete draft or outline, when a story is "fine scene by scene but doesn't add up," or when the user asks "does the whole thing hold together?"

worldbuilding-critic.name: worldbuilding-critic
worldbuilding-critic.description: Judge whether an invented system — a magic system, an economy, a society, a technology — is actually SOUND, not merely internally consistent. Use after the consistency audit passes, when a world-bible needs a quality verdict, when designing or stress-testing a fantasy/SF system, or when the user asks "does this magic system / faction structure hold up?" Emits a diagnosis of the offending axioms and un-propagated consequences, never a score.

scheherazade.name: scheherazade
scheherazade.description: Meta-orchestrator for the agentic world→character→story loop. Generates (or extends) a fictional world, its characters, and a story set in it by driving the worldbuilding and writing domains over one shared world-state, closed by the critic suite (consistency + quality + macro) with human checkpoints at the creative forks. Use to generate a world and a story end-to-end, or to draft quality-gated prose grounded in an existing world-bible. Not for single-skill asks (just worldbuild or just draft) — those route to the domain orchestrators.

day-trader.name: day-trader
day-trader.description: Opening-range breakout intraday trader. After the first 15 minutes of RTH, watches for breakouts above the opening high (long) or below the opening low (short — disabled in v1, cash account) with VWAP confirmation. Hard exit by 15:55 ET. 5-minute tick cadence during RTH. Use when asked "what does the day trader say" or "intraday setup on X". Default review-only.

dca-investor.name: dca-investor
dca-investor.description: Dollar-cost-averages a fixed weekly tranche of notional into a broad-ETF basket. Equity-only, cash-account safe. No conviction calls, no market timing, no exits — just a metronome. Use when the user asks "DCA into X", "set up automated buying", "schedule weekly investments", or "what does the DCA strategist say". Default mode is review-only; live mode requires explicit promotion.

earnings-event-trader.name: earnings-event-trader
earnings-event-trader.description: Post-earnings drift fade strategist. Identifies allowlist names that just reported an EPS BEAT but gapped DOWN ≥2% — irrational reaction setup. Buys on the gap, exits at +3% or 5 trading days. Equity-only in v1; an options variant lives in options-strategist. Use when user asks "earnings setups today", "did X beat", or "what does the earnings trader see". Review-only default.

executor.name: executor
executor.description: The single broker-tool gate for the strategist suite. Strategists hand it an Intent[] payload; it runs pre-flight, validates against SOUL invariants, applies run-context routing (cron / interactive chat / Claude Code), calls review_equity_order (and place_equity_order in cron+live), and returns RealizedAction[]. NEVER invoke this skill directly from chat — strategists call it via the Skill tool. Direct invocation produces undefined behavior.

macro-overlay-trader.name: macro-overlay-trader
macro-overlay-trader.description: Dalio-quadrant macro overlay. Asks regime-intelligence which growth×inflation quadrant we're in and rotates a small SPY/TLT/IEF/GLD basket to the corresponding target weights. Monthly cadence, plus off-cadence on regime shift. Composes both regime-intelligence and asset-universe. Use when user asks "what regime are we in for positioning", "macro overlay view", or "how should I tilt the book". Default review-only.

options-strategist.name: options-strategist
options-strategist.description: Single-leg options strategist focused on income generation — cash-secured puts (CSP) on quality names you'd be happy to own, and covered calls (CC) against existing positions. EXPLICITLY ISOLATED from the autotrader profile (equity-only per SOUL); runs only as a Claude Code analyst or in a future dedicated options-trader profile with its own SOUL. Capability-gated to option_level_2+. Use when user asks "CSP setup on X", "covered call ideas", or "options income". Default review-only.

rebalancer.name: rebalancer
rebalancer.description: Maintains a target asset-weight basket via drift-triggered rebalancing. Emits both buy and sell intents (the only strategist in v1 that sells). Monthly cadence by default; off-cadence ticks fire only if drift exceeds the panic threshold. Use when the user asks "rebalance my book", "am I overweight X", or "bring me back to target". Default mode is review-only.

reflexivity-trader.name: reflexivity-trader
reflexivity-trader.description: Soros-style reflexive position trader. Heavily composes the reflexivity-sentiment director to identify adoption-validation feedback loops in real-time narratives (AI capex, obesity drugs, etc.), then sizes by the director's reported conviction. Weekly cadence, ≤30 day holds. Use when user asks "is X a reflexive setup", "narrative trade ideas", or "what does the reflexivity trader see". Default review-only.

swing-trader.name: swing-trader
swing-trader.description: RSI(14) mean reversion on a small allowlist of liquid large caps. Buys oversold (RSI<30), exits at RSI>70 or after 10 days. Conviction-scaled sizing. Daily cadence; many ticks no-op. Use when the user asks "swing trade ideas", "is X oversold", or "what does the swing trader say". Default review-only.

conflict-design.name: conflict-design
conflict-design.description: Design a conflict — war, insurgency, revolution, cold or economic conflict, feud — as a system: why it starts, how it escalates, what equilibrium holds it, how it ends, and how it corrupts its participants. Reference when building the central conflict of a world or story, a war between factions, a rebellion, or a rivalry. Covers the five conflict axes (each a stated/felt dual), conflict as a metastable game tipped by emotional variance, and the strategist who manages the variance gradient.

south-asia.name: south-asia
south-asia.description: Analyze South Asia as a connected historical zone covering the Indus civilization, the Vedic and classical ages, the Sultanate and Mughal empires, the colonial Raj, and the modern republics. Use when examining region-specific dynamics including caste and social order, religious plurality and its politics, the northwest gateway, the Indian Ocean monsoon world, and the contested question of Indian civilizational unity.

southeast-asia.name: southeast-asia
southeast-asia.description: Analyze Southeast Asia as a connected historical zone spanning the mainland kingdoms (Vietnam, Angkor, Burma, Siam) and the maritime world (Srivijaya, Majapahit, the archipelago). Use when examining region-specific dynamics including Indianization vs Sinicization, mandala polities, the upland-lowland divide, the spice trade and plural colonialisms, and the twentieth-century wars of decolonization.

visualization.name: visualization
visualization.description: Direct the visualization subdomain — route a data-communication need to the right specialist: single-chart messaging, at-scale or interactive dashboards, or narrative data storytelling. Use when the user needs to choose a chart, build a dashboard, render large data, or tell a story with data. Resolves conflicts between clarity, scale, and narrative.

interactive-dashboards.name: interactive-dashboards
interactive-dashboards.description: Build interactive, at-scale, and real-time data visualizations. Reference when choosing a rendering technology by data volume (SVG vs Canvas vs WebGL/WebGPU), selecting a 2026 charting framework (ECharts, Recharts, Visx, Nivo, deck.gl, Vega-Lite, Plotly), designing dashboards with linked views and progressive disclosure, or handling streaming and embedded analytics.

data-storytelling.name: data-storytelling
data-storytelling.description: Design data narratives — sequence visualizations into a story that holds attention and lands a decision. Use when turning a set of charts into an argument, building a scrollytelling piece or data-driven report, pacing a guided reveal, choosing annotation-as-message, or adapting a narrative across dashboard, presentation, and report contexts.

decision-journal.name: decision-journal
decision-journal.description: Persists purchase research and learns from outcomes: appends research runs to data/decision-journal.jsonl, purchases and 30-day check-ins to data/purchases.jsonl, maintains data/consumer-preferences.json, and mirrors briefs into the user's Obsidian vault via vault-writer when reachable. Use at the start of an emptor run (recall priors), at its end (persist the brief), and when /purchase-log or /purchase-review fire. Closes the calibration loop by resolving brief confidence against real satisfaction.

emptor.name: emptor
emptor.description: Orchestrates rigorous consumer purchase research from need to verified recommendation. Use when the user wants to buy something and asks "what's the best X", wants product options compared, or needs purchase claims verified — any consumer buying decision across electronics, appliances, software, services, and beyond. Runs requirements elicitation before any prices are seen, searches only trusted sources, verifies finalists, scores them on the user's own weighted criteria, and journals the outcome for calibration.

needs-elicitor.name: needs-elicitor
needs-elicitor.description: Interviews a buyer before any product research happens: jobs-to-be-done framing, MoSCoW must-haves, deal-breakers, and a budget locked before any price is seen. Use when starting a purchase decision and the real requirements are not yet pinned down — emptor's elicit phase, or standalone when someone says "help me figure out what I actually need". Produces a signed-off requirements spec with weighted criteria; performs no web searching itself.

product-verifier.name: product-verifier
product-verifier.description: Verifies a shortlisted product's hard facts before it can be recommended: marketing claims against independent test data, current availability and discontinuation status, recall and reliability history, and merchant trustworthiness for purchase links. Use during emptor's verify phase on each finalist, or standalone when the user asks "is this product's claim actually true?" or "is this store legit?".

recommendation-brief.name: recommendation-brief
recommendation-brief.description: Assembles the final EMPTOR BRIEF for a purchase decision and runs its pre-flight audit: ranked pick with confidence-and-because clauses, trade-off map, evaluation matrix, sensitivity, forensics flags, trust-checked merchants, freshness stamps, and the feedback footer. Use during emptor's brief phase after evaluation completes, or standalone to re-render an existing evaluation into the brief contract. Rejects and regenerates rather than delivering an unauditable brief.

review-forensics.name: review-forensics
review-forensics.description: Scores the authenticity of a product's review corpus using a five-signal ensemble (velocity, verified-purchase ratio, rating distribution, account patterns, cross-product repetition). Use when evaluating whether crowd reviews for a specific product can be trusted as evidence — typically during emptor's verify phase, or standalone when the user asks "are these reviews fake?". Returns a per-product authenticity verdict, never a guess: signals that cannot be checked are reported as unchecked.

source-trust-atlas.name: source-trust-atlas
source-trust-atlas.description: Maps consumer review sources to trust tiers and routes product categories to the sources worth searching. Use when planning where to research a purchase, deciding how much weight a review source deserves, or checking whether a review is too stale to trust. Called by emptor during the source-plan phase; also useful standalone when the user asks "which review sites can I trust for X?".

house-policy.name: house-policy
house-policy.description: The committed investing parameters — scope, authority, position-cap hierarchy, risk gates, factor targets, and the amendment procedure. Use before any sizing, rebalancing, or risk-limit decision, and whenever a strategist or Archon proposes an action. This file holds decided values, not ranges or advice; where it is silent, no policy exists yet and the answer is "unstated", never an improvised default.
